_about: NCAA Division I baseball tournament history 2015-2026 (no 2020 tournament). Compiled 2026-10-27. The bracket data (national seeds, regional seeds 1-4, regional and super-regional winners, MCWS teams, finalists, champion, automatic qualifiers) was parsed from the raw wikitext of the Wikipedia pages '<YEAR> NCAA Division I baseball tournament' (8TeamBracket templates and bid tables). Checks: 64 unique teams per year, 16 regionals, champion among the CWS teams, national seeds = hosts from 2018, automatic qualifiers all appear in the field. Super-regional 'national_seeds' are the bracket seed labels (null = unseeded); 'series' is games won by teams[0]-teams[1], counted from game scores. Regional 'site' is the Wikipedia regional name (2026 Morgantown regional was actually in Granville, WV). Team names are Wikipedia short names with ' State' converted to ' St.' (NC State kept), plus a few aliases (Connecticut->UConn, Southern Miss->Southern Miss., Louisiana-Lafayette->Louisiana, LIU Brooklyn/Long Island->LIU). Conference names are shortened (SEC, ACC, CAA, CUSA, MAAC, MAC, SoCon, SWAC, WAC, MEAC, ASUN). Rules come from the NCAA 2025-26 and 2024-25 Division I Baseball Pre-Championship Manuals, NCAA.com (16-seed change, Oct 2017), the ABCA/collegebaseballdaily coverage of the 2013 RPI change, and Baseball America (Jan 2024 selection changes).

rules.field: 64 teams in every year 2015-2026. Automatic bids (conference champions) by year: 31 in 2015-2019 and 2022; 30 in 2021 (Ivy League did not compete), 2023 and 2024 (MEAC no longer sponsored baseball); 29 in 2025 and 2026 (Pac-12 lost its automatic bid after realignment). At-large = 64 - automatic: 33 (2015-2019, 2022), 34 (2021, 2023, 2024), 35 (2025, 2026). Counts derived from the Wikipedia automatic-bid tables; the 2026 NCAA pre-championship manual states 29 automatic qualifiers.
rules.national_seeds_change: The NCAA Division I Competition Oversight Committee approved moving from 8 to 16 seeded teams starting with the 2018 championship (announced Oct. 6, 2017). Before that, teams 9-16 were not seeded, so the No. 1 seed could meet the 9th-best team in a super regional. From 2018, super regionals are set up so that seed 1 meets seed 16 if both advance, 2 meets 15, and so on.
rules.regional_format: 16 four-team double-elimination regionals over Friday-Monday, starting the Friday after Memorial Day. Day 1: G1 No.1 vs No.4, G2 No.2 vs No.3. Day 2: G3 loser G1 vs loser G2 (elimination), G4 winner G1 vs winner G2. Day 3: G5 winner G3 vs loser G4, G6 winner G4 vs winner G5. Day 4: G7 if necessary (same teams as G6). The bracket pairings cannot be changed once the tournament starts. The No. 1 seed in each regional is its host, with exceptions when a team's park does not meet NCAA requirements (2015 UCSB at Lake Elsinore; 2019 Oklahoma St. at Oklahoma City because of flooding; 2021 Old Dominion's regional played at South Carolina).
rules.super_regional_format: 8 best-of-three series between pairs of regional champions, played Friday-Sunday or Saturday-Monday (four supers start each day). The higher national seed hosts if it submitted an acceptable bid; otherwise the lower seed hosts if its bid is acceptable. If neither team is a national seed (equal seeding), the committee picks the host from the bids based on facility, revenue and similar factors. Before 2018 only the 8 national seeds were guaranteed to host a super if they advanced (e.g., 2015 Missouri St. could not host because of a venue conflict).
rules.cws_format: Eight teams at Omaha (Charles Schwab Field, formerly TD Ameritrade Park). Two four-team double-elimination brackets; the two bracket winners play a best-of-three final (MCWS Finals). This format was unchanged in 2015-2026. The 2026 manual schedules the finals as single games Saturday, Sunday and Monday (if necessary), June 20-22, with the MCWS beginning the Friday after super regionals.
rules.super_regional_pairing: 2018-2026 (16 seeds): the 64-team bracket is set so that if all 16 No. 1 regional seeds advance, the super regionals would be 1 vs 16, 2 vs 15, 3 vs 14, 4 vs 13, 5 vs 12, 6 vs 11, 7 vs 10 and 8 vs 9 (2026 pre-championship manual). Each super pairs the two regionals in that slot regardless of who wins them. 2015-2017 (8 seeds): each national seed's regional was paired with one unseeded host's regional; pairings were mainly geographic/committee choice with no published 9-16 order. These supers fed the MCWS as 1 vs 8, 4 vs 5 (one bracket) and 2 vs 7, 3 vs 6 (other bracket), as seen in the 2015-2017 brackets (observed pattern, not a written rule found).
rules.cws_bracket_pairing: The MCWS brackets follow the two halves of the 64-team bracket. One bracket gets the winners of the supers in the 1/16, 8/9, 4/13 and 5/12 slots, and the other gets 2/15, 7/10, 3/14 and 6/11. Opening games are the 1/16 winner vs the 8/9 winner, 4/13 vs 5/12, 2/15 vs 7/10 and 3/14 vs 6/11. Every 2018-2026 bracket on Wikipedia matches this. Wikipedia's 'Bracket 1'/'Bracket 2' labels do not always follow it: in 2023 the 1/16 half (Wake Forest) is labeled Bracket 2. In the 8-seed era the halves were national seeds 1, 8, 4, 5 and 2, 7, 3, 6.
rules.regional_placement: From the 2026 pre-championship manual (the 2025 manual has the same wording): half of the field (32 teams) is seeded in four groups of 1-8. The committee picks the top 32 teams; the top 16 are ranked in order and become the regional No. 1 seeds/hosts, and teams 17-32 are the regional No. 2 seeds. Once seeds are set they do not change during bracketing. Apart from the 32 seeded teams, regionals are filled by closest geography to the sites whenever possible. Teams may be moved out of their region to balance the bracket, or when an out-of-region opponent is about as close and would make a better competitive matchup. Teams from the same conference are placed in different regionals. The committee does not reseed after the bracket is set. Regional host criteria: on-campus or approved site; national balance (preferably at least one regional in each of the five D-I baseball regions); minimum financial guarantee of $75,000 (75% of estimated net receipts); lights highly recommended; permanent restrooms; past crowd behavior considered. Seeded teams may host if they meet requirements and bid by the deadline (Bylaw 31.1.3.2.5). Since 2018 the 16 regional hosts are the 16 national seeds (exception: 2021 Old Dominion). In 2015-2017 the 8 national seeds plus 8 other committee-chosen hosts held the 16 regionals. The manual does not say how No. 2 seeds (17-32) are matched to specific No. 1 seeds; this is largely geographic in practice.
rules.selection_criteria: Bylaw 31.3.3 general criteria: won-lost record; strength of schedule; eligibility and availability of student-athletes. Baseball-specific factors (2025/2026 manuals, 'not necessarily in priority order'): overall record; Division I record; overall RPI rank; nonconference record and RPI rank; conference regular-season record and conference tournament results; road record and RPI; record in four RPI quadrants by game location (Q1: home vs RPI 1-25, neutral 1-40, away 1-60; Q2: home 26-50, neutral 41-80, away 61-120; Q3: home 51-100, neutral 81-160, away 121-240; Q4: home 101+, neutral 161+, away 241+); last 15 games; head-to-head; common opponents; input from regional advisory committees. Quadrants and the KPI were added for the 2024 selections (Baseball America, Jan. 2024); earlier years used results vs RPI top 25/50/100-style tiers. At-large teams must be better than .500 against Division I opponents. Only countable games vs four-year varsity teams count, and the RPI uses Division I games. RPI formula: 25% the team's winning percentage + 50% opponents' winning percentage + 25% opponents' opponents' winning percentage. Since the 2013 season the team's own winning percentage is weighted by location: road win = 1.3, neutral win = 1.0, home win = 0.7; road loss = 0.7, neutral loss = 1.0, home loss = 1.3. This is based on home teams winning about 62% of D-I games. The NCAA also uses an 'adjusted RPI' with a bonus/penalty structure, mainly for notable nonconference wins and losses; the values are not published. Other metrics: the Kevin Pauga Index (KPI) has been a resource since 2024, explicitly 'not a selection criteria'. NEW for 2026: Diamond Sports Rankings (DSR), a predictive metric, was added to the team sheets as a resource (approved by the Baseball Oversight Committee). As of the 2026 manual the RPI formula itself is unchanged. No NET-style replacement of the RPI had been adopted for baseball by 2026.
rules.selection_dates_note: Selection Monday (Memorial Day). The bracket show is at noon ET (2026 on ESPN2); regional hosts are announced the day before. Dates for 2018-2026 come from Wikipedia ('announced on the Selection Show on ...'); 2015 is from ABC/AP news, 2016-2017 from AP and Oxford Eagle; 2026 is from the 2026 pre-championship manual.

regionals.note: Old Dominion was the No. 1 seed but could not host at its own park (facility did not meet NCAA requirements); regional played at South Carolina's Founders Park with South Carolina as host institution.

2021.note: No 2020 tournament (COVID-19). Ivy League did not play in 2021, so 30 automatic bids. Old Dominion (No. 11 national seed) played its regional at South Carolina. One MCWS game (Vanderbilt vs NC State) declared a no-contest and NC State eliminated under COVID-19 protocols.

regionals.note: Oklahoma State hosted at Chickasaw Bricktown Ballpark in Oklahoma City due to flooding in Stillwater.
UCSB was the host/No. 1 seed but its home stadium did not meet requirements; played at neutral Lake Elsinore Diamond.

2015.note: 8 national seeds; Missouri St. (No. 8) could not host a super regional because of a venue conflict (its super was played at Arkansas). UC Santa Barbara hosted its regional at Lake Elsinore.
